## Best Ollama alternative for Mac, Windows and Linux

| OS | Pick | Why |
 --- 
| macOS | LM Studio or mlx-lm | LM Studio’s MLX engine runs MLX models on Apple Silicon behind a desktop app; mlx-lm runs and quantizes MLX models from Python |
| Windows | LM Studio or Jan | Both ship Windows apps with an OpenAI-compatible local server, on port 1234 and port 1337 |
| Linux | llama.cpp with llama-swap, or vLLM | llama-swap switches between several llama.cpp models behind one endpoint; vLLM serves multi-user traffic on GPU servers |

On a Mac, llama.cpp also fits if you want Metal builds you compile yourself. On Windows, llama.cpp’s llama-server covers CUDA and Vulkan builds. vLLM does not support Windows natively, so keep it on Linux servers.

## LM Studio vs Ollama for Local LLM Work [...] ### What is the best Ollama alternative for Mac?

The best Ollama alternative for Mac is LM Studio, whose MLX engine runs MLX-format models on Apple Silicon behind a polished desktop app and local server. For a Python workflow, mlx-lm runs and quantizes MLX models directly from Hugging Face. llama.cpp is the pick if you want Metal builds you compile and control yourself.

 

### What is the best Ollama alternative for Windows?

The best Ollama alternative for Windows is LM Studio or Jan, since both ship Windows desktop apps with a local OpenAI-compatible server on ports 1234 and 1337. Jan is open source under Apache 2.0 and adds MCP tools and cloud model connectors. For CUDA or Vulkan builds, run llama.cpp's llama-server instead.

 

### Is Ollama still relevant? [...] LocalAI (MIT): an open-source AI engine that runs LLMs, vision, voice, image and video models on any hardware, with no GPU required.
 llama-swap (MIT): swaps models on demand in front of llama.cpp, vLLM or any local OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible server.
 llamafile (Apache 2.0, now under mozilla-ai): distributes and runs an LLM as a single file.
 SGLang (Apache 2.0): an inference framework for large language, vision-language and diffusion models, optimized for agentic workloads and large-scale serving.
 KoboldCpp (AGPL-3.0): runs GGUF models locally from one file with a KoboldAI UI and zero install.
 GPT4All (MIT): runs local LLMs on desktop machines; its latest release, v3.10.0, shipped in February 2025.

## Why this exists: the Mac app, ported

Hugging Face describes Llama Windows as the Windows counterpart to llama.app on macOS, and the repository calls it a WinUI 3 port of Llama for Mac. That lineage explains the design: a small menu-style app that stays out of the way, a curated model list, and a local server other tools can point at. The ggml team maintains llama.cpp itself, so the app tracks the engine closely, and the shared Hub cache means the three layers (engine, app, Hub) use the same files instead of duplicating gigabytes of weights. Llama Windows is a free, open-source app that puts llama.cpp in the Windows 11 system tray. Hugging Face announced it on October 13, 2026, written by Morgan Funtowicz, Jeff Boudier and Emanuil Rusev, with the code in the ggml-org organization. It manages llama.cpp for you, downloads models from the Hugging Face Hub in one click, and serves an OpenAI-compatible API on localhost. It also launches with native support for Windows on Arm and NVIDIA's RTX Spark. We covered the hardware side in our post on the RTX Spark launch software; this post is the dedicated look at the app. For the chip, see the RTX Spark power specs.
